meta.name: Expose CRM read/write tools to Claude and ChatGPT via a gated MCP server

name: Gate every AI write with a policy engine and audit log in an n8n MCP server

parameters.toolDescription: Look up one customer record by name or account ID. Returns owner, tier, region and contact details. Use this before any write so you are acting on the right account.
Get the status, ship date and value of one order by its order ID.
List unpaid invoices for one customer, with amounts and due dates. Read only.

parameters.description: Record a note against a customer account. Goes through the policy gate: empty notes are refused, anything resembling a credential is redacted, and an identical note inside the same hour is rejected.
Create a follow-up task for a customer. Put a YYYY-MM-DD due date inside details. The policy gate refuses due dates in the past.
Draft a customer email in Gmail. It is only ever a DRAFT and is never sent. Put the recipient address inside details. The policy gate refuses addresses outside the allowed domains.
Post a message to the account team in Slack. The policy gate refuses an identical message inside the same hour, so a looping model cannot spam the channel.

parameters.content:
## Gate every AI write with a policy engine and audit log in an n8n MCP server

### Why this exists
Hooking an assistant up to your business systems is the easy part. The hard part is that the moment it can write, it can write anything - to anyone, twice, with whatever it hallucinated in the arguments. Most MCP servers hand over raw table access and hope.

This one puts a gate in front of every write, and writes down what happened either way.

### How it works
The MCP trigger publishes seven tools to any MCP client - Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, or an AI Agent in another n8n workflow.

The three read tools answer questions directly: look up a customer, check an order, list a customer unpaid invoices. They cannot change anything.

The four write tools do not touch your systems at all. Each one calls this same workflow back through its Execute Sub-workflow trigger, so every write - note, task, email draft, Slack message - funnels through one policy engine before anything happens.

That policy engine is a Code node you own and can read end to end. It refuses unknown actions and missing fields. It redacts anything shaped like an API key or bearer token before it can be written into your sheets. It refuses email drafts to domains outside your allow list. It refuses task due dates in the past. And it fingerprints each request in workflow static data, so a model stuck in a loop cannot log the same note or page the same channel twice within an hour.

Whatever passes is routed to the real action. Emails are only ever drafted, never sent. Every attempt, allowed or refused, is appended to an audit sheet with the action, the customer, who asked for it, the verdict and the reason.

Finally the model is told the truth about what happened: what was done, or exactly what was refused and why, and that a draft still needs a human. It is never left to assume a blocked write succeeded.

### Setup
1. Connect Google Sheets, Gmail and Slack, and create a Header Auth credential holding a long random token.
2. In the four guarded tool nodes, set Workflow to THIS workflow so the gate can call itself.
3. Point the tools at your spreadsheet. Tabs needed: Customers, Orders, Invoices, Notes, Tasks, AI Audit Log.
4. Open Check the Policy and edit ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS and the limits at the top to match your business.
5. Activate, copy the MCP URL from the trigger, and add it to your client with the same token header.

### Customization tips
Add your own rules to the policy engine - a spend ceiling, a working-hours window, a block on named accounts. Add a new action with one Switch branch and one entry in REQUIRED. Remove any write tool you do not want the model to have at all.

## 1. The MCP surface
One token-protected endpoint publishes seven tools. The three on the left only read - a customer record, an order, a customer unpaid invoices. The four on the right are writes, and none of them touches your systems directly: each calls this workflow back through the policy gate below.

## 2. One gate every write must pass
The Code node is the whole point, and it is yours to read and edit. Unknown actions and missing fields are refused. Anything shaped like an API key is redacted before it can be written. Email drafts to domains outside your allow list are refused, as are due dates in the past. Repeat requests are fingerprinted in static data, so a looping model cannot log the same note or page the same channel twice within the hour.

## 3. Act, record, and tell the model the truth
Whatever passes is routed to the real action - emails are drafted, never sent. Allowed or refused, every attempt is appended to the audit sheet with the verdict and the reason. The model is then handed a plain answer: what was done, or exactly what was blocked and why, so it never reports a refused write as a success.
